strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas GH#66722 (and related GH#66699) where assert_series_equal/assert_almost_equal with check_dtype=False, check_exact=False, rtol=0, atol=0.5 incorrectly passes for large mixed int/float values (float64 cannot represent the 1-integer difference). Build pandas from the buggy commit 8cb88cf1fbd0, then run the specific util tests added in the PR diff to ensure the test suite fails on buggy and passes on fixed.

build_commands: python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel
pinned_because: NumPy is numerically relevant, but no minimum/maximum version constraint was provided in the evidence; therefore do not pin an exact NumPy version unless your local test matrix already does. Instead, select a NumPy version supported by your pandas checkout that reproduces the float64 precision regime (e.g., any NumPy using IEEE-754 float64).
Cython is required to build pandas from source (documented in README excerpt).

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/util/test_assert_series_equal.py::test_assert_series_equal_large_mixed_integer_float_atol (and optionally test_assert_series_equal_large_mixed_integer_float_rtol) as shown in the provided PR diff.
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (pandas commit 8cb88cf1fbd0), the test(s) that expect an AssertionError for atol=0.5 with check_dtype=False, check_exact=False, rtol=0 will FAIL because tm.assert_series_equal does not raise (wrong_value: it incorrectly treats the values as equal). On the fixed revision (the PR that implements GH#66722/GH#66699 behavior), the same tests will PASS because the code path applies atol/rtol to exact integer values instead of short-circuiting via array_equivalent after casting large ints to float64.
strategy.numerical_probe: Compare int64/uint64 values around 2**60+1 or 2**63+1 to float64 values float(2**60) / float(2**63); float64 cannot represent the 1-integer difference, so tolerance logic must not be bypassed.

input_output_examples.input: left = pd.Series([2**60 + 1], dtype="int64"); right = pd.Series([float(2**60)], dtype="float64"); pd.testing.assert_series_equal(left, right, check_dtype=False, check_exact=False, rtol=0, atol=0.5)
input_output_examples.expected_output: AssertionError: Series are different (because abs difference 1 > atol 0.5 with rtol 0)

risks: This bug is sensitive to the mixed integer/float comparison path that short-circuits via array_equivalent after converting/casting large integers to float64; if your environment uses a different dtype-coercion behavior, the wrong short-circuit might not occur.

The evidence does not provide specific minimum NumPy versions; since NumPy is unbounded in the provided context, you must rely on any supported NumPy that uses IEEE-754 float64. A very old/new NumPy could alter casting/representation corner cases (low likelihood but possible).

The evidence does not state C compiler/toolchain requirements; building from source may fail or behave differently on certain platforms/compilers. If you cannot build pandas with the provided build commands, the reproduction cannot transition.

Some PR tests also include nullable dtypes (Int64/Float64 with pd.NA) but the core failure is described for pure int64/float64. If nullable-dtype behavior differs, restrict to the explicit int64/float64 cases in the test.

If the fixed code is only present on a different PR commit than the one you check out, ensure you checkout the actual fix commit/branch; otherwise the “passes_on_fixed” state may not be reached. (The evidence provides the buggy commit hash but not the fixed commit hash.)

oracle.why: The tests assert raising/not raising and sometimes a specific error message. The oracle for success is behavioral (AssertionError raised) rather than numeric equality; tolerance correctness is embedded in the test parameters (rtol=0, atol=0.5).

strategy.fails_on_buggy: pandas/tests/util/test_assert_series_equal.py::test_assert_series_equal_large_mixed_integer_float_atol expects tm.assert_series_equal(...) to raise AssertionError for the pair [2**60+1] (int64) vs [float(2**60)] (float64) with check_dtype=False, check_exact=False, rtol=0, atol=0.5. On the buggy revision, the call does not raise due to early short-circuit after casting large integer to float64, so the test’s `with pytest.raises(AssertionError, match="Series are different"):` block fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After applying the fix from PR #66722, the same tm.assert_series_equal call raises AssertionError under atol=0.5 (abs difference 1 > atol), and the second call with atol=1 succeeds, matching the test expectations.
